## Left open by the earlier read (RD-025)

An independent reader judged the previous rewrite of this lesson. Fix everything below as well. Each item is as serious as an item under "Fix these".

### Findings

1. Rule L02 (Major). Problem: The teaching uses the advanced word “binomials” without explaining it. That breaks the very-simple Grade 5 prose requirement even though the rest of the multiplication method is plain.
   > To multiply complex numbers, multiply each term as you would with two binomials. Then replace every $i^2$ with $-1$ and combine the real terms and the $i$ terms.
2. Rule L22a (Minor). Problem: This paragraph has four sentences. The formatting rule limits lesson paragraphs to one to three short sentences.
   > A **complex number** has the form $a+bi$, where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers. The number $a$ is the **real part**, and $b$ is the **imaginary part**. If $b=0$, the number is real. If $a=0$ and $b\ne0$, it is purely imaginary.
3. Rule L25 (Major). Problem: The method depends on the unexplained term “binomials.” A student needs that meaning before this sentence can serve as the promised multiplication teaching.
   > To multiply complex numbers, multiply each term as you would with two binomials. Then replace every $i^2$ with $-1$ and combine the real terms and the $i$ terms.
